story.head: Stamkos’s favorite opponent
paras: The Wild won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Nashville on Oct 1. The Wild have won three straight, the last a 6-2 rout of Boston. The Predators (11-5-5) lost 4-2 to San Jose on Sunday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Preds third (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Wild first (tied for second).

The Predators’ record (.643) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.539), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. So is the Wild’s (.773 on chances worth .638), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Wild (32nd) and the Predators (31st) both get pinned in their own end on long shifts. The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest). The Wild draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.18 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Predators. Beyond that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Predators (3rd), so expect an open game.

Filip Forsberg (7 G / 16 A / 23 P in 21 GP) leads the Predators in scoring. Steven Stamkos (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 21 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for seventh in the NHL, with a point in nine straight games against Minnesota. Kirill Kaprizov (17 G / 20 A / 37 P in 22 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. Quinn Hughes (7 G / 23 A / 30 P in 22 GP) is next in line, with eight points in his last five games.

Juuse Saros (7-4-4 / .917 SV% in 15 GS) has been a rock in net for Nashville and is expected to start. Jesper Wallstedt (14-2-3 / .926 SV% in 19 GS) has been a rock in net for Minnesota and is expected to start.
The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.
